label: Milk powder
comment: Dried from a concentrate, not from evaporated milk.

about.text: Powdered milk, also called milk powder, dried milk, dry milk, or milk solids, is a manufactured dairy product made by evaporating milk to a state of dryness. One purpose of drying milk is to preserve it; milk powder has a far longer shelf life than liquid milk and does not need to be refrigerated, due to its low moisture content. Another purpose is to reduce its bulk for the economy of transportation. Powdered milk and dairy products include such items as dry whole milk, nonfat (skimmed) dry milk, dry buttermilk, dry whey products and dry dairy blends. Many exported dairy products conform to standards laid out in Codex Alimentarius.

how.text: Pasteurised milk is boiled down under vacuum to about half solids, then sprayed as a fine mist into hot air, where the water leaves in a moment and a dry powder falls out. It keeps unchilled because it holds so little water.

steps.note: Between evaporation and drying, to cut the free fat in the powder.
Preheated from 10 to 80 °C to set its viscosity before it is atomised.
Sprayed into hot air that enters at 200–220 °C and leaves at 75–80 °C.
